audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart contradicts its own prose in the first three rows. It scores Level 1 'Skill' and Levels 2-3 'Singed', while content early opens 'Sett wins levels 1 and 2 cleanly', whys[0] says stay out of auto range, and whys[1] says 'let him push and farm safely under tower'. It then scores Levels 4-5 and Level 6 'Skill' while the same prose calls 4-5 'your proxy window' and says 'At 6 Insanity Potion flips the 1v1'.
audit.why: Emerald+ 54.28% over 1380 games — Singed is comfortably ahead, but the shape is late, not early. Sett with Knuckle Down and Pit Grit beats a Singed who has no Mega Adhesive yet; from the proxy window on, Sett has no dash and cannot catch him. The packet chart reads Sett, Sett, Skill, Singed, Singed, Singed, Singed and matches the prose exactly.
audit.corrected: Chart moved as one group to Sett, Sett, Skill, Singed, Singed, Singed, Singed across both layers, with phases[0..4].why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spikes are in the right places but the packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing cues in this matchup — every 'trade around Haymaker's cooldown' line is numberless.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, Knuckle Down 9/8/7/6/5s and The Show Stopper 120/100/80s. Haymaker's 18s at rank 1 is the longest basic-ability gap in the lane and it is the one that decides whether a proxy run-past is free.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, phases[3].why, phases[4].why, whys[2] and wants.you[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Two flatly false claims, both about the same thing. spikes[2]: 'Insanity Potion's armor and magic resist absorb Haymaker's true-damage center.' whys[4]: 'Insanity Potion's armor and MR absorption shaves Haymaker's true-damage core to survivable.' Also whys[0] attributes Grit storage to Pit Grit, and whys[2] claims Mega Adhesive cancels the Haymaker cast.
audit.why: True damage is by definition unreduced by armour and magic resist, so Insanity Potion's resistances do nothing at all against Haymaker's centre — what it actually gives you against Sett is health, regen and the move speed to leave. Riot's Haymaker text puts the storage on W itself: 'Sett passively stores damage he takes as Grit', while Pit Grit is the alternating-punch passive plus missing-health regen. And Mega Adhesive slows and grounds; nothing in its description interrupts a cast, so 'the W cast is cancelled' is not supported. The real interaction the page should be selling is the one it half-states: Fling displaces Sett, and Fling into Mega Adhesive roots him inside a live Poison Trail while Haymaker sits on 18s.
audit.corrected: spikes[2], whys[0], whys[2], whys[4], wants.you[1], dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d, report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemisation advice implicitly rewards stacking resistances into a champion whose signature ability deals true damage in the centre.
audit.why: Against Haymaker the answer is maximum health and positioning to the side lobes, which take physical damage, not the centre. The _missing rule for this pair says the same: Sett bypasses stacking resistances, so raw armour or MR reads the trade wrong.
audit.corrected: Folded into report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns rather than a separate item line.

notes: Left alone deliberately: content late says 'disengage before The Show Stopper's suppress cooldown resets'. Riot's text describes Sett carrying a champion through the air and slamming them, which is a displacement rather than a named suppression, and I could not verify the suppression wording from the kit data — the 120s figure is in breakdown.cooldowns instead. Also unverified and therefore not written: whether Fling actually interrupts a Haymaker cast. Fling demonstrably displaces him, so I wrote that his punch lands where you are not, which is true either way.
